review_status: AI-assisted source reviewed; independent human source review pending; not frozen
label_policy: Direct = likely implementation edit target. Indirect = dependent behavior or an existing regression test exercising the affected behavior. Retrieval-relevant = useful context, not automatically impacted. Potential = plausible relationship without enough evidence for confirmed impact. Labels are source-backed hypotheses, not instructions to edit every listed file.

cases.requirement: Reject article create and update API requests when the title exceeds 120 characters.

annotations.rationale: ArticleInCreate.title and ArticleInUpdate.title at line 28 are currently unrestricted strings; request validation belongs here.
Create and update endpoints at lines 60 and 96 consume the request schemas, so their accepted input behavior changes.

context_annotations.rationale: The domain Article has a title field, but the requirement is limited to API request validation.
Existing create and update tests use short titles; no test asserts the new 120-character boundary.

potential_impacts.rationale: Could require a domain constraint if the rule is later extended beyond API inputs.

ambiguities.note: The current requirement does not say whether internal Article construction must enforce the same length limit.

cases.requirement: Use underscores instead of hyphens in title-derived article slugs on create and title update.

annotations.rationale: get_slug_for_article currently delegates to slugify without a separator override; this is the slug generation edit target.
Create calls get_slug_for_article here and title update calls it again at line 100; both route outputs depend on the generated slug.
The update test explicitly expects the hyphenated slug new-title and would need to reflect the requested separator.

context_annotations.rationale: The repository persists the slug passed by the route; the selected requirement does not establish a repository edit.
The SQL update stores new_slug and existing links may depend on stored slugs, but migration policy is unspecified.

potential_impacts.rationale: Existing persisted slugs or inbound links may need migration or compatibility handling if the product requires it.

ambiguities.note: No migration or backwards-compatible lookup behavior for existing hyphenated slugs is specified.

cases.requirement: Raise the default API page size for article lists and user feeds from 20 to 30, without changing explicit limit requests.

annotations.rationale: DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and is the shared API default constant.
The list endpoint's limit query parameter imports the shared default constant.
The feed endpoint's limit query parameter also imports the shared default constant.
The list endpoint depends on get_articles_filters at line 32 and passes its resolved limit to the repository at line 40; changing the shared API default changes omitted-limit behavior.

context_annotations.rationale: Repository methods have separate default argument values of 20, but API callers pass limit explicitly.
The feed test requests the default and then an explicit limit, but its small result set does not assert 20 versus 30.

potential_impacts.rationale: Internal direct callers would still see 20 unless repository defaults are also changed; the requirement is API-scoped.

ambiguities.note: Whether repository method defaults should also become 30 depends on whether the requirement covers non-API callers.

cases.requirement: Shorten issued JWT access tokens from one week to 24 hours.

annotations.rationale: ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is one week and is passed to token creation at line 31.
Login and registration at line 81 issue access tokens through this helper, so returned token lifetime changes.
Current-user and update responses at line 61 also issue access tokens through the same helper.
Protected-request authorization decodes JWTs at lines 84-91; newly issued 24-hour tokens are rejected sooner when their expiry is reached.

context_annotations.rationale: The test creates a user token and checks username only; it does not assert expiry duration.

potential_impacts.rationale: A new expiry-boundary regression test should be added, but the existing assertion does not encode the one-week policy.

cases.requirement: Replace the configured Authorization scheme prefix Token with Bearer for protected API requests.

annotations.rationale: jwt_token_prefix is configured as Token; replacing that setting is the likely implementation edit.
Protected routes compare the supplied prefix with the configured prefix, so accepted requests change.

context_annotations.rationale: The wrong-prefix test uses WrongPrefix, which remains invalid; it does not verify a valid Bearer token.
The authorization_prefix fixture reads the configured prefix, so test setup follows the setting automatically.

potential_impacts.rationale: A new test for valid Bearer and rejected Token prefixes is needed; current tests do not encode that migration.

ambiguities.note: If a transition period accepts both Token and Bearer, this comparison becomes a direct edit target; the requirement says replace.

cases.requirement: Allow an article author to delete comments on their article even when another user wrote the comment.

annotations.rationale: The permission predicate currently allows only the comment author; it needs the article-owner rule and article context.
The delete permission dependency calls that predicate without article context at line 43 and raises 403.
The delete endpoint depends on the permission check; authorized behavior changes without requiring a route body edit.
The existing test expects 403 for another user's comment on test_article, which is authored by the requesting user.

context_annotations.rationale: test_article is created with test_user as author; authorized_client uses that user's token at line 85.
The repository deletes by comment id and comment author's username; it does not itself check the requesting user's identity.

ambiguities.note: The exact function signature is design-dependent; article context is already available in get_comment_by_id_from_path at line 18.

cases.requirement: Reject blank or whitespace-only comment bodies at the comment creation API boundary.

annotations.rationale: CommentInCreate.body is an unrestricted string at line 16; API validation belongs in this request schema.
The create endpoint consumes CommentInCreate before passing its body to the repository, so request acceptance changes.

context_annotations.rationale: The repository accepts a body string, but the requirement specifies only the API boundary.
The existing creation test submits a nonblank body and does not test blank rejection.
The response/domain Comment body is a plain string and need not be constrained for API-only validation.

potential_impacts.rationale: Would matter if the blank-body policy is later required for all internal Comment construction.

cases.requirement: Make repeated POST requests to favorite an already-favorited article return the unchanged article with HTTP 200 instead of HTTP 400.

annotations.rationale: The favorite POST branch raises HTTP 400 when article.favorited is already true; response construction must handle the unchanged state.
The parameterized test explicitly expects HTTP 400 for a repeated favorite POST and must be updated for this new contract.

context_annotations.rationale: Favorite insert already uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so duplicate persistence does not establish a SQL edit.
The repository calls the existing insertion query; the route rejects the duplicate before reaching it.

ambiguities.note: The existing test is parameterized for POST and DELETE; only the POST expectation changes under this requirement.

cases.requirement: Reject current-user profile update API requests when bio exceeds 160 characters.

annotations.rationale: UserInUpdate.bio is an optional unrestricted string; the API payload limit belongs in this request schema.
The current-user update endpoint consumes UserInUpdate before persisting the bio at line 59.

context_annotations.rationale: The domain bio field is a string; API-only validation does not require changing it.
The repository accepts bio and persists it, but the requirement is scoped to API requests.
The existing profile update test uses a short bio and does not assert the new boundary.

potential_impacts.rationale: Could be affected if the product later requires all internal user records to obey the same limit.

cases.requirement: Change rounding of invoice totals in billing reports to banker's rounding.

negative_evidence.rationale: The included API router registers users, profiles, articles, comments, and tags, with no billing or invoice route.

cases.negative_rationale: The complete selected app/ and tests/ trees in the snapshot manifest contain no billing, invoice, or report component. This is a negative case only for the selected snapshot, not a claim about outside code.
